findings.summary: The spec and progress-rule docstring overstate repeat handling when command text is unavailable.
evidence: In `ProgressRule._on_complete`, a missing command takes the `if not command` branch, increments `_new_outcomes`, and returns. Repeated unnamed completions therefore each count as progress, including with an unreadable worktree.

The spec says that with an unreadable tree “a rerun is not” progress, without limiting that claim to commands whose text is known; the progress-rule docstring similarly says rerunning a command on an unchanged tree is not new.
findings.action: Qualify the spec and docstring: repeated completions count as non-progress only when command text is available to identify the repeat. Otherwise, change the implementation and add a regression test.

counterweight_triage.concern: C-B1: deferred request delivered on a known repeat with an unreadable tree
counterweight_triage.disposition: The code checks for a deferred request and no remaining in-flight commands before returning for an unreadable fingerprint. The new regression test covers delivery at that completion; the change is localized.

counterweight_triage.concern: C-A3: later no-progress stop identifies commands it interrupts
counterweight_triage.disposition: The stop reason includes the currently in-flight command text (or an unnamed-command placeholder), and the regression test asserts the interrupted command appears.

counterweight_triage.concern: C-A1, C-A2, C-A4: debug follow-up fallback and naming claims
counterweight_triage.disposition: The notes scope lane-token routing to names outside main/master/trunk/develop, describe the slug and branch hash behavior, and identify the reftable `.invalid` placeholder as a counter fallback. These claims match the helper and selected tests.

next_move: Qualify the unnamed-command repeat behavior in the spec and docstring, or change the code and test it, before release lock-in.
